# Ask Alexa+ to Read Your Calendar Aloud and Get a Heads-Up Before Meetings

> **In short:** Link a Google or Microsoft calendar to Alexa in the Alexa app, then ask any Echo "what's on my calendar today?" to hear your meetings read out loud. Turn on Calendar Notifications and Alexa+ will announce upcoming events on the Echo you choose.

Say one short sentence to your Echo in the morning and you'll hear today's meetings read out — with times, titles, and any details you've saved in the event itself. No phone, no typing, no scrolling. This guide walks a complete beginner through linking a calendar, picking the right voice command, and setting automatic reminders before each meeting.

## Before you start
- An Echo device (Echo Dot, Echo Show, or similar) or the Alexa app on a phone.
- A free Amazon account, signed in on both the device and the app.
- A Google or Microsoft calendar that already has at least one event on it.
- An Alexa+ subscription. Pricing, bundled offers and availability change often and differ by country — check Amazon's site in your region for the latest. In the US, Alexa+ is included with Prime, and separate plan options may also be available. The calendar features described here require an Alexa+ subscription.
- About 5–10 minutes for the first-time setup, then roughly 10 seconds per morning.

## Step 1 — Link your calendar to Alexa

Open the Alexa app on your phone, tap **More**, then **Settings**. Select **Preferences**, then **Calendar**. Choose your account provider (for example Google or Microsoft), tap **Continue**, and follow the on-screen instructions to sign in with the account that holds your events. Repeat these steps for each calendar you want to link.

Each person in the household can link their own calendars, and you can set a default personal calendar as well as a shared family calendar.

💬 Example: if your meetings live in your work account, link that one too — not only the calendar with holidays or family events.

You'll know it worked when Alexa can read out one of your real events in Step 3.

## Step 2 — Make sure your Echo is awake and listening

Place your Echo somewhere you'll be in the morning — kitchen counter, bedside table, or desk. The light ring around the top should be **off** or glowing soft **blue**; that means Alexa is ready but not yet talking. If the ring is **red**, the microphone is muted — press the small microphone button on top once to unmute. If you don't own an Echo, open the Alexa app and tap the Alexa button in the app; it listens through your phone's mic.

💬 Example: Say *"Alexa, hello"* as a quick test. You should hear a short chime and a friendly spoken reply.

On devices with a screen (Echo Show), a thin blue light bar along the bottom edge does the same job the top ring does on a regular Echo.

You'll know it worked when Alexa answers your test question out loud — that confirms the microphone, speakers, and account are all wired up correctly.

## Step 3 — Ask Alexa+ to read today's meetings

Say clearly: *"Alexa, what's on my calendar today?"* A short chime plays, then Alexa+ starts reading each event in order — the time, the event title, and any details you've saved inside the entry (a location, a video-call link, an agenda note). Exactly which details are spoken back depends on what you put into the event itself. If today is empty, Alexa+ will say something like "You have no events scheduled for today."

💬 Example: *"Alexa, what are my meetings today?"* and *"Alexa, read my schedule"* work just as well. *"Alexa, what's next on my schedule?"* gives you only the very next event.

If Alexa+ answers with "I can't access your calendar" or "Please link a calendar first," go back to Step 1 — the link didn't take. Try unlinking and re-linking the account once.

You'll know it worked when you hear your real meetings read out loud, in the right order, with the correct times.

## Step 4 — Turn on calendar notifications before meetings

Alexa+ can announce your upcoming events on an Echo device you choose. To opt in, open the Alexa app and tap **More** → **Settings** → **Calendar** → **Calendar Notifications**, then follow the on-screen instructions.

Amazon's help doesn't say how far ahead these announcements come, so listen to the first one and see whether the timing works for you. If you want a warning at an exact time, set an ordinary reminder by voice instead.

💬 Example: *"Alexa, remind me to join my call at 9:50."*

If you've set up Alexa Voice ID, the notifications and your personal calendar are tied to your voice, so each family member hears their own events.

You'll know it worked when your chosen Echo announces an upcoming event from your calendar.

## Step 5 — Make it a one-sentence morning habit

Pick one phrase and use it every day. Alexa+ can summarize your day, tell you how busy it will be, and find free time slots. Amazon's own example is *"What does my day look like tomorrow?"* — the same works for today.

💬 Example: *"Alexa, what does my day look like today?"*

If you notice a mistake while it reads, you don't need to open your calendar app: Alexa+ can add events, change an event's date, time or title, or delete it — just ask.

You'll know it worked when you hear your whole day in one answer while you keep getting ready.

## Common mistakes
- **Skipping the calendar link.** The most common reason "Alexa, what's on my calendar?" fails is that no calendar is linked yet. Open the Alexa app → More → Settings → Preferences → Calendar and connect a Google or Microsoft account before you start asking.
- **Linked the wrong calendar.** If you have multiple Google calendars (work, personal, family, holidays), Alexa+ only reads the one you picked. Open the app, check the selected default, and switch it if needed.
- **Asking while the mic is muted.** A red light ring means Alexa cannot hear you. Press the microphone button on top once and wait for the ring to turn blue before you speak.
- **Forgetting that others can hear it.** Amazon notes that content from a linked calendar might be available to anyone using your Alexa devices. Keep private appointments in a calendar you don't link, or set up Voice ID.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** Say one sentence while brushing your teeth and hear the full day out loud — no screen, no scrolling, no notifications buried under twenty other apps. Handy for parents juggling school runs, drivers on the way to work, visually impaired users, or anyone who simply prefers listening.
- **For your work or business:** Use it to never walk into a meeting unprepared. An announcement before each meeting gives you time to find the link, open the right tab, and skim the agenda. Teams running back-to-back calls lose several minutes a day to "wait, what's next?" — this removes that.
- **If you're just getting started:** Don't try to set reminders for every meeting at once. Link the calendar, ask once, and only add a reminder if you actually need it. Small steps beat over-engineering.

## Try it now
Open the Alexa app, link your Google or Microsoft calendar, then walk up to any Echo in your home and say: *"Alexa, what's on my calendar today?"* — that's the whole first move. If it works, turn on **Calendar Notifications** tomorrow (More → Settings → Calendar).
